After ChatGPT users were limited only by weekly usage caps over the past few weeks, OpenAI announced today that it will restore the five-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Details below.

The five-hour usage cap restoration applies to ChatGPT Plus subscribers

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering at OpenAI, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus subscribers will see the return of the five-hour usage limit, applicable to Codex and ChatGPT Work.

Once users hit the five-hour or weekly usage cap, they can choose to wait for the next cycle to reset their usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI sometimes also resets user caps for free, and users can also earn backup reset credits through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI temporarily lifted the five-hour usage limits for Codex and ChatGPT Work, retaining only the weekly caps.

During that period, the company also reset users' weekly usage several times early to celebrate milestones, including reaching one million more active users across the two (now unified) platforms.

However, as Tibo explained on X tonight:

Tomorrow we will restore the five-hour usage limit on Plus accounts for ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this earlier, but then postponed it. (a) The five-hour limit helps us spread out the compute load, allowing for a more generous weekly usage plan; (b) Most Plus plan users are casual and new users, and they sometimes accidentally burn through their entire weekly allowance, get confused, and end up having a poor experience. Over the coming months, the $100 and $200 Pro subscriptions will not have the five-hour limit enabled.

Tibo did not mention any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate, credits-based usage system.

Will the return of the five-hour usage limit for ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
